tools.name: check_paper
tools.description: Look up one paper in the OpenRepro ledger and return its re-run outcome with its qualifiers (such as a broad bound or a check that missed), how many agent-designated controls were excluded and how many gates the test had (when it has any), how many headline claims held, the assurance level, and link

tools.name: search_reports
tools.description: Search published re-runs by words in the title, authors, venue or field, optionally filtered by outcome or field. With no query, lists the whole ledger.

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: The full public record for one paper: outcome and qualifiers, summary, assurance, the attempt history (released and superseded versions with reasons), every claim checked with the published value, the re-run value, the registered tolerance, the check kind and the verdict, plus evidence links.

tools.name: how_to_verify
tools.description: The log's final hash, the downloadable evidence bundle, the report's SHA-256 from the release manifest, and the one command that checks the bundle with only Python. The verifier checks log and artifact integrity and that the report names the log's head hash; it does not check the report's contents a

tools.name: request_rerun
tools.description: For a paper not yet in the ledger: returns a ready-to-send email link to OpenRepro with the request filled in. Nothing is sent or stored by this tool; the user sends the email if they want to.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_paper · Private data: get_report · Public sink: request_rerun · Destructive: check_paper, get_report.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_paper · Private data: get_report · Public sink: request_rerun · Destructive: check_paper, get_report

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
